infl_ens.data.trait_space¶

Trait-space construction for the influencer-game router.

Builds an \(L\)-dimensional trait space \(\mathbb{B}\) together with an empirical resource distribution \(B(b)\) from a corpus of queries. The space is constructed automatically: queries are embedded by a user-supplied encoder, projected onto a low-dimensional space (either via interpretable anchor directions or via PCA), scaled to \([0, 1]^L\), and the resource density is estimated by Gaussian kernel-density estimation on a uniform grid.

This module is data-prep only: no disk I/O, no global state.

References:

Lovett & Fu (2024). “Learning Dynamics of the Influencer’s Game in Resource Landscapes.” See in particular §2 (Influencer’s Game Model) and Fig. 1d–e (LinkedIn job-market construction).

class infl_ens.data.trait_space.TraitSpace(grid, weights, project, axis_labels=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

A discretised trait space \(\mathbb{B}\) with an empirical resource distribution.

Parameters:

  • grid (numpy.ndarray) – Trait grid points, shape (K, L). K is the number of discretisation points and L is the trait dimensionality.

  • weights (numpy.ndarray) – Resource weights \(B(b_k)\) at each grid point, shape (K,), normalised to sum to one.

  • project (Callable[[Sequence[str]], numpy.ndarray]) – Callable mapping a sequence of raw query strings to their coordinates in \(\mathbb{B}\), returning shape (M, L). Used at routing time to embed live queries.

  • axis_labels (tuple[str, ...] | None) – Optional human-readable labels for the L axes (e.g. ('math', 'code', 'creative')).

infl_ens.data.trait_space.build_trait_space(queries, encoder, *, anchors=None, L=3, n_grid=32, kde_bandwidth=None)[source]¶

Construct a trait space and resource distribution from a query corpus.

The pipeline is:

  1. Embed queries via encoder.

  2. Project to L dimensions, either by cosine similarity to anchors (interpretable axes) or by PCA (data-driven axes).

  3. Min-max rescale to \([0, 1]^L\).

  4. Lay an n_grid-per-axis uniform grid.

  5. Estimate \(B(b)\) by isotropic Gaussian KDE on the grid.

Parameters:

  • queries (Sequence[str]) – Calibration corpus. Should be representative of the live query distribution.

  • encoder (Callable[[Sequence[str]], numpy.ndarray]) – Callable mapping a list of strings to an (N, D) embedding matrix.

  • anchors (Sequence[str] | None) – Optional list of anchor concept strings. If supplied, its length determines L and produces interpretable axes.

  • L (int) – Trait-space dimensionality. Ignored when anchors is given. Keep \(L \in \{2, 3, 4\}\) so the \(n_{\text{grid}}^L\) grid stays tractable; switch to a codebook for larger L.

  • n_grid (int) – Number of grid points per axis.

  • kde_bandwidth (float | None) – Optional KDE bandwidth in trait-space units. If None, Scott’s rule \(n^{-1/(L+4)}\) is used.

Returns:

A TraitSpace carrying the grid, normalised resource weights, and a project callable for runtime query embedding.

Return type:

TraitSpace

Raises:

ValueError – If len(queries) < 2 * L or L < 1.

infl_ens.data.trait_space.position_from_corpus(queries, project, *, scores=None)[source]¶

Estimate an agent’s position in trait space from a corpus of queries.

Returns the trait-space centroid of queries after projection, optionally weighted by scores (e.g. per-query benchmark accuracy or reward). This is the standard way to observe where a model lives in \(\mathbb{B}\), in contrast to choosing positions strategically.

Typical uses:

  • Initial position from base-model behaviour: pass queries the base model handles well; the centroid is the model’s current “centre of mass” in trait space.

  • Post-training update: after a round of fine-tuning, pass the training corpus (or an eval set with per-query scores) to re-estimate where the model now sits.

Parameters:

  • queries (Sequence[str]) – Queries to embed and average. Must be non-empty.

  • project (Callable[[Sequence[str]], numpy.ndarray]) – Trait-space projector from TraitSpace.

  • scores (Sequence[float] | None) – Optional per-query non-negative weights of shape (len(queries),). If None, a uniform mean is taken. If all scores are zero, falls back to the uniform mean.

Returns:

Position vector, shape (L,).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – If queries is empty or scores has the wrong shape.
